guidance.summary: Equinor raised its 2026 production growth guidance from 3% to about 4% and kept its capital returns, including a USD 3bn buyback. Offsetting this, coverage of the quarter is mixed on whether profit beat or missed, and the CFO flagged softer 2027 production and a later Empire Wind start.

CFO said 2027 production should not be fully in line with 2026; Empire Wind first power in H1 2027, a bit later than planned.

writeup.headline: Equinor rates Hold at 64, one point below Buy, on strong momentum offset by a weaker balance sheet.
writeup.thesis: Equinor scores 64, a Hold that sits just 1 point below the Buy band. The strongest driver is trend (91): the price is 27.6% above its 200-day average, shares are up 78.0% from 12 months ago to 1 month ago, and the price is only 2.4% below its 52-week high. Quality scores 64 on an operating margin of 23.8% and a diluted share count down 8.0% year on year, though the FCF margin is a thinner 5.6%. Growth is middling at 54, with TTM revenue growth of 2.6%, although growth sped up by 5.8 pp from the previous quarter. The balance sheet is the weak spot at 38 (net debt to FCF of 3.52, cash to debt of 0.19), and valuation could not be scored because the foreign-filer price and share data were not reconciled.
key_risks: Balance sheet is the weakest factor: net debt is 3.52 times FCF and cash covers only 0.19 of debt.
After a large run-up, with the price 27.6% above its 200-day average, the shares are exposed to a pullback if oil and gas prices soften.
The CFO flagged softer 2027 production and a later Empire Wind start, and coverage of the quarter is mixed on whether profit beat or missed.
The FCF margin of 5.6% is thin relative to the 23.8% operating margin.
Revenue growth is modest, with TTM revenue growth of 2.6%.
what_would_change: A gain of just 1 point, for example from firmer revenue growth or a better balance sheet score, would lift the rating to Buy.
A fade in momentum would pull down the trend score of 91, which is the main support for the current score.
A drop of 20 points would be needed to reach Sell, which would likely require weaker growth, quality and trend together.
Negative news on production guidance, Empire Wind or analyst downgrades would lower the news score of 65.
